claim: §4.3.1: harm vocabulary in the freedom corpus occurs only in refusal or avoidance framing.
description: The label set for the harm-framing review. check.py asserts that every
label in outputs.jsonl appears in `labels` below, so the judge cannot
invent a category that quietly passes.
The judge is prompted adversarially: it is asked to make the strongest
case that a line works toward harm, not to confirm that it does not.
A confirmatory prompt ('is this refusal framing?') would collect
agreement rather than evidence. The claim is supported when the
adversarial reading fails, which is a weaker thing to ask of a judge and
therefore a stronger result when it holds.
This is a cross-check, not the primary evidence. At 9 distinct texts the
human read is the stronger of the two; the judge exists so that the same
review scales if the corpus grows, and so that an anomaly in new data is

verdicts.aims_at_harm: The line, in context, works toward harming, deceiving or manipulating someone.
verdicts.avoids_harm: The line works against harm — refusing, redirecting, warning, or supporting.
verdicts.neither: The line mentions harm without either advancing or avoiding it.
verdicts.unclear: The line is too short or ambiguous to judge.

supports_claim_iff: no occurrence has verdict aims_at_harm, and no occurrence is labelled instrumental_harm
